description:
## Goal

Make recursive structural meaning finite without constructing an ever-deeper concrete Ty ladder. The tuple and list nesting reproducers must terminate with bounded semantic work while preserving every runtime answer and every type distinction promised by the supported denotational domain.

## Proven root problem

The current immutable structural Ty language has no recursive-equation binder. Semantic construction eagerly embeds operand Ty children, so recursive families such as T = :start | {int, T} expand inline forever. Activation-key count and return-widening budgets do not bound the cost: one activation can repeatedly construct deeper inputs.

Finite source syntax does not imply finitely many exact input classes. id(x) = x must remain parameterized rather than join unrelated callers. A recursive same_depth(a,b) can distinguish every nesting depth, so independent per-input finite partitions are unsound.

## Model gate

Before production changes, examine existing LoweredBody, type interning, callable and pattern representations. Prove the smallest supported recursive or parameterized denotation algebra and its decidable operations. LoweredBody remains the sole source computation authority; owner-qualified references may borrow its operands, constructors, calls and outcomes but copy no body meaning.

State exactly which answers are exact and where approximation is sound. A wrapper that recursively reinterprets arbitrary bodies, a second flow graph, a BDD copy, inline expansion, arbitrary depth or row caps, and widen-after-construction are rejected.

Projection may avoid constructing children only when the consumer question does not observe them. Returned denotation requires a recursive equation, parameterized result or an explicit sound abstraction; it may not silently discard structure.

## TDD and signal

Vary nesting depth while source shape stays fixed for tuple and list accumulators. Bound activation keys, recursive summary nodes, Ty constructions, comparisons, fact movements and formula evaluations on interp, JIT and AOT.

Prove identity, projection and construction wrappers across callers with distinct nested inputs do not cross-pollute returns. Exercise same_depth, repeated versus distinct operands, correlated rows and ordered nested matches. FIFO, LIFO and permuted admission produce identical semantic answers and artifacts. No hidden inline type ladder may precede a stable final key.

## Deletion and acceptance

Delete the return/input ascent ladder, arbitrary construction budgets and obsolete termination claims only when replaced by the proved model. Do not preserve a compatibility type authority. Full focused, corpus, three-door, deterministic, documentation, formatting, check and strict-Clippy gates pass; fresh ticket-scoped cold review precedes one commit and close.

## BLOCKED BY

- ◐ fz-tfn.62 P1 Keep callable identity through quoted source; delete canonical-name re-resolution

## UNBLOCKS

- ○ fz-kdt.64 P1 Retain exactly the supported semantic alternatives


Aggravating case, 2026-09-15 (fixtures2/behavior/json_roundtrip.fz on fz-acn/one-plan-fact at ac2543eb9, the goal program; counts from --log-telemetry, magnitudes from sample on the plain binary, because the stream's own rendering inflates span times on this fixture, fz-t75). Json.value/1's ReturnType at arrow 64 is revised 18 times and never converges: define_return (src/compiler2/semantic.rs ~1132) tops out at any past 2 * RETURN_WIDENING_BUDGET = 16 ascents, and the backend dump shows Json.value/1, Json.val/1, Json.decode/1 and Json.array_element/2 all returning fp[any] any, the answer available on rung one. Twelve ReturnType facts sit at 15-18 revisions. Each revision wakes every caller through a current ReturnType dependency: 990 of the 1233 AnalyzeActivation wakes are ReturnType; AnalyzeActivation runs 77 times for Json.array_element/2, 55 for Json.decode/1, 32 for Json.object_colon/3, 59 for main/0; 54% of all 4527 jobs are re-runs; 380 activations for 140 functions. The fixture's JSON nests three deep, so the ladder is the value union growing a member per rung and then nesting, with the list-only ADDRESS_COLLAPSE_DEPTH leaving map nests uncapped. The erased any returns then cost a second time downstream: 315 deliver_lanes shims and 314 resume continuations are 57% of the 1110 functions Cranelift compiles, which is the other third of the lane (fixpoint drive about 65% of 3.5s on an M4, Cranelift about 35%, the program's own run under 0.2%). Signal for the fix: ReturnType revisions of Json.value/1 in single digits and its return a finite recursive denotation rather than any; AnalyzeActivation runs per activation in single digits; deliver_lanes and resume counts falling with them. Distill with tools/distill-telemetry.exs.

comments.text: LIST VARIANT of the same class (fz-kdt.183 cold review, 2026-09-03): `fn nest(acc, n), do: (if n == 0, do: acc, else: nest([acc], n - 1))` with nest([], 2) hangs (rc=124 at 40s) at 0889c0b3a for every n in {2,3,4,5,6,8}; the non-nesting control terminates in milliseconds. A self-nesting accumulator element -- tuple (this ticket) or list -- defeats the documented termination theorem in type-specialization.md:123-135 (no numeric singletons, finite atoms, return-join widening: none bounds element NESTING). Unaffected either way by 183's element-keyed prototype.

CONCORDANT with fz-kdt.65 (the RETURN_WIDENING_BUDGET side of the ladder): the budget counts strict ascents of the RETURN; a nesting accumulator ascends the INPUT key per rung with a super-linear Types cost per rung, so neither the return budget nor ACTIVATION_INPUT_ROW_BUDGET ends it in time. Note in .agent/docs/type-specialization.md:123-135 the termination carriers (no numeric singletons, finite atoms, return-join widening) do not name element nesting.

Measured (fz-kdt.177.2 review, json_roundtrip at 2d5f79d07): standalone semantic drive settles at 277 activations with a return revision / 843 analyses / max 9 revisions / 0 widened; the product pull every door takes reaches 380 activations / 1476 analyses / max 17 / 5 widened, and the three SHARED arrow-64 keys (Json.decode/1 9→17, val/1 8→17, value/1 8→17) climb the extra rungs. The pull's 103 extra activations are what feed the extra evidence into the shared returns: the ladder length is driven by the activation population, not by a demand edge on Json.value/1. Prediction for the kernel: a recursive denotation collapses the population and the ladder in one motion; the activation count (380 → ~126) and the revision count are one signal, not two.

title: Represent recursive denotations without expanding infinite type ladders
